result.topic_en: Latin supplement to §40 of Jacobi's Fundamenta nova: termwise-integrated q-series for log k, log k', log(2K/π) and related functions, first as series of logarithms and then expanded in powers of q using divisor sums.
result.transcription:
Additamenta ad §m. 40. (Fundamenta nova. Jacobi)
Formulae in hoc §o propositae, in eo casu ubi modulus ipsius $q$ unitatem aequat consideratione satis dignae videntur quippe quae functiones unius variabilis pro quovis argumenti valore discontinuas praebeant [-sistant-]
Series quidem propositae magna ex parte pro modulo ipsius $q$ unitati aequali non convergunt sed integrando series convergentes inde derivari possunt; itaque primo integralia formularum 1 – 7 proponimus [-exhibemus-]
48.) $\int_0^q (\lg k - \lg 4\sqrt{q})\frac{dq}{q} = -4\lg(1+q) + \frac{4}{4}\lg(1+q^2) - \frac{4}{9}\lg(1+q^3) + \frac{4}{16}\lg(1+q^4) + \cdots$
49.) $\int_0^q -\lg k'\frac{dq}{q} = 4\lg\frac{1+q}{1-q} + \frac{4}{9}\lg\frac{1+q^3}{1-q^3} + \frac{4}{25}\lg\frac{1+q^5}{1-q^5} + \frac{4}{49}\lg\frac{1+q^7}{1-q^7} + \cdots$
50.) $\int_0^q \lg\frac{2K}{\pi}\frac{dq}{q} = 4\lg(1+q) + \frac{4}{9}\lg(1+q^3) + \frac{4}{25}\lg(1+q^5) + \cdots$
51.) $\int_0^q \left(\frac{2K}{\pi}-1\right)\frac{dq}{q} = -4\lg(1-q) + \frac{4}{3}\lg(1-q^3) - \frac{4}{5}\lg(1-q^5)\cdots$
$= 2i\lg\frac{1-qi}{1+qi} + \frac{2i}{2}\lg\frac{1-q^2i}{1+q^2i} + \frac{2i}{3}\lg\frac{1-q^3i}{1+q^3i} + \cdots$
52.) $\int_0^q \frac{2kK}{\pi}\frac{dq}{q} = 4\lg\frac{1+\sqrt{q}}{1-\sqrt{q}} - \frac{4}{3}\lg\frac{1+\sqrt{q^3}}{1-\sqrt{q^3}} + \frac{4}{5}\lg\frac{1+\sqrt{q^5}}{1-\sqrt{q^5}} - \cdots$
[-53.) $\int(\frac{2kK}{\pi})\frac{dq}{q}$-] $= 4i\lg\frac{1-i\sqrt{q}}{1+i\sqrt{q}} + \frac{4i}{3}\lg\frac{1-i\sqrt{q^3}}{1+i\sqrt{q^3}} + \frac{4i}{5}\lg\frac{1-i\sqrt{q^5}}{1+i\sqrt{q^5}} + \cdots$
53.) $\int_0^q\left(\frac{2k'K}{\pi}-1\right)\frac{dq}{q} = -4\lg(1+q) + \frac{4}{3}\lg(1+q^3) - \frac{4}{5}\lg(1+q^5) + \cdots$
$= -2i\lg\frac{1-qi}{1+qi} + \frac{2i}{2}\lg\frac{1-q^2i}{1+q^2i} - \frac{2i}{3}\lg\frac{1-q^3i}{1+q^3i} + \cdots$
54.) $\int_0^q\left(\frac{2\sqrt{k'}K}{\pi}-1\right)\frac{dq}{q} = -\frac{4}{2}\lg(1+q^2) + \frac{4}{6}\lg(1+q^6) - \frac{4}{10}\lg(1+q^{10}) + \frac{4}{14}\lg(1+q^{14}) - \cdots$
$= -\frac{2i}{2}\lg\frac{1-q^2i}{1+q^2i} + \frac{2i}{4}\lg\frac{1-q^4i}{1+q^4i} - \frac{2i}{6}\lg\frac{1-q^6i}{1+q^6i} + \frac{2i}{8}\lg\frac{1-q^8i}{1+q^8i}$
ubi logarithmos ita sumendos esse manifestum est, ut evanescant posito $q=0$.
Functiones eaedem ad dignitates ipsius $q$ evolutae adhibitis Cl. Jacobi {+(Fundamenta pag. 105)+} denotationibus hoc modo repraesentantur.
55. $\int_0^q(\lg k - \lg 4\sqrt{q})\frac{dq}{q} = -4\sum_p \frac{\varphi(p)}{p^2}\left(q^p - \frac{3q^{2p}}{4} - \frac{3q^{4p}}{16} - \frac{3q^{8p}}{64} - \frac{3q^{16p}}{256} - \cdots\right)$
56. $\int_0^q -\lg k'\frac{dq}{q} = 8\sum_p\frac{\varphi(p)}{p^2}q^p$
57. $\int_0^q \lg\frac{2K}{\pi}\frac{dq}{q} = 4\sum_p\frac{\varphi(p)}{p^2}\left(q^p - \frac{1}{2}q^{2p} - \frac{1}{4}q^{4p} - \frac{1}{8}q^{8p} - \frac{1}{16}q^{16p} - \cdots\right)$
(ubi summae ad dextram ad omnes numeros impares positivos $p$ sunt extendendae et $\varphi(p)$ denotat summam divisorum ipsius $p$.)
58. $\int_0^q\left(\frac{2K}{\pi}-1\right)\frac{dq}{q} = 4\sum\frac{\psi(n)\,q^{2^\lambda(4m-1)^2 n}}{2^\lambda(4m-1)^2 n}$
59). $\int_0^q\frac{2kK}{\pi}\frac{dq}{q} = 8\sum\frac{\psi(n)\,q^{\frac{(4m-1)^2 n}{2}}}{(4m-1)^2 n}$
(60) $\int_0^q\left(\frac{2k'K}{\pi}-1\right)\frac{dq}{q} = -4\sum\frac{\psi(n)\,q^{(4m-1)^2 n}}{(4m-1)^2 n} + 4\sum\frac{\psi(n)\,q^{2^{\lambda+1}(4m-1)^2 n}}{2^{\lambda+1}(4m-1)^2 n}$
61). $\int_0^q\left(\frac{2\sqrt{k'}K}{\pi}-1\right)\frac{dq}{q} = -4\sum\frac{\psi(n)\,q^{2(4m-1)^2 n}}{(4m-1)^2 n} + 4\sum\frac{\psi(n)\,q^{2^{\lambda+2}(4m-1)^2 n}}{2^{\lambda+2}(4m-1)^2 n}$
(denotante $n$ numerum imparem cujus factores primi omnes sunt formae $4\mu+1$, $\psi(n)$ numerum factorum ipsius $n$. Quae quidem formulae etiam e formulis 27 – 33 [-Cl. Jacobi-] §i 40 in Fundamentis novis a Cl. Jacobi datis per integrationem derivari possunt.

methods.what: Termwise integral of log(k/4√q) as series of logarithms
Integral of -log k' as series of logarithms
Integral of 2K/π−1 in two logarithmic forms
Power series of the integral of log k' via divisor sum φ(p) over odd p
Power series of the integral of log(k/4√q) with divisor sums
Power series of integral of log(2K/π)
Power series of integral of 2K/π−1 using ψ(n), number of divisors of n with all prime factors ≡1 mod 4
Method: integrate divergent series termwise to obtain convergent series on |q|=1
methods.quote: sed integrando series convergentes inde derivari possunt; itaque primo integralia formularum 1 – 7 proponimus

items.quote: Formulae in hoc §o propositae, in eo casu ubi modulus ipsius $q$ unitatem aequat consideratione satis dignae videntur quippe quae functiones unius variabilis pro quovis argumenti valore discontinuas praebeant
items.english: The formulae proposed in this section seem quite worthy of consideration in the case where the modulus of q equals unity, since they yield functions of one variable that are discontinuous for every value of the argument.

items.quote: Series quidem propositae magna ex parte pro modulo ipsius $q$ unitati aequali non convergunt sed integrando series convergentes inde derivari possunt
items.english: The proposed series for the most part do not converge when the modulus of q equals unity, but convergent series can be derived from them by integration.

items.quote: Quae quidem formulae etiam e formulis 27 – 33 [-Cl. Jacobi-] §i 40 in Fundamentis novis a Cl. Jacobi datis per integrationem derivari possunt.
items.english: These formulae can also be derived by integration from formulae 27–33 of §40 given by the celebrated Jacobi in the Fundamenta nova.
